passage.title: The Storm
paras: The storm did not arrive; it invaded. It marched over the hills in grey columns, flattened the barley, and hammered at every shutter in the village. Inside the bakery, Amira pressed her palm against the trembling glass and watched the street surrender, one gutter at a time.

The bell above the door jangled as old Mr Farouk stumbled in, rain streaming from his beard. 'The bridge,' he gasped. 'The river is over the bridge.' Amira's father was already reaching for his coat. Outside, the wind screamed down the chimney, and somewhere a shutter tore free and clattered away into the dark.
